mainTopic: Teaching Torah to a daughter, and the meaning of חסיד שוטה and רשע ערום in the משנה
overview: The גמרא goes back to the end of the משנה, where בן עזאי says a father must teach his daughter Torah and רבי אליעזר objects. The גמרא first softens רבי אליעזר's harsh wording to 'as if' he taught her תיפלות. רבי אבהו then gives his source, 'אני חכמה שכנתי ערמה': wisdom brings cunning with it. The רבנן read the same פסוק as teaching that Torah lasts only in someone who 'strips himself bare' for it, and רבי יוחנן adds that Torah lasts only in a truly humble person. Next the גמרא explains רבי יהושע's line that a woman prefers less food with her husband's closeness over more food with separation. It then defines the people the משנה says wear away the world. A חסיד שוטה is a man who won't save a drowning woman because he would have to look at her. Several אמוראים give different definitions of a רשע ערום, from clever legal tricks to hypocrisy, and עולא's definition continues on the next amud.

steps.title: בן עזאי and רבי אליעזר on teaching a daughter Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. בן עזאי says a father must teach his daughter Torah, and רבי אליעזר says that doing so is teaching her תיפלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי says: A person must teach his daughter Torah. רבי אליעזר says: Anyone who teaches his daughter Torah is teaching her promiscuity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the two opposing opinions from the משנה so it can start discussing them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי's reason in the משנה is that a סוטה should know that a זכות can delay her punishment. רבי אליעזר strongly disagrees and says Torah learning will harm the daughter. The rest of the sugya explains his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Promiscuity, foolish or lewd behavior
'Etc.', meaning the rest of the quote from the משנה is assumed

phrases.english: Ben Azzai says:
A person is obligated to teach, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה is: a person must teach his daughter Torah.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Anyone who teaches his daughter Torah
is teaching her promiscuity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹמֵר בֶּן עַזַּאי: חַיָּיב אָדָם לְלַמֵּד אֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן עזאי: one must teach his daughter Torah. רבי אליעזר: teaching her Torah is teaching her תיפלות.

steps.title: Can Torah really be called promiscuity?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by רבי אליעזר's wording. How could Torah itself be called תיפלות?
steps.simpleTranslation: Could you really think it is promiscuity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the literal wording of רבי אליעזר, because Torah cannot actually be promiscuity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is on the wording, not on רבי אליעזר's opinion itself. Torah is holy, so calling the Torah being taught 'תיפלות' cannot be meant literally.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Would it enter your mind?' A way of saying an idea is impossible

phrases.english: Promiscuity, could it enter your mind?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיפְלוּת סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the literal wording of רבי אליעזר's statement in Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'מלמדה תיפלות' in רבי אליעזר's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Torah is holy wisdom, so it cannot literally be תיפלות.

steps.title: Read it as 'as if' he taught her promiscuity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: it is as if he taught her תיפלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: it is as if he taught her promiscuity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by adding the word 'כאילו', meaning 'as if'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah itself is not תיפלות. The result of teaching her, though, is just as bad as if he had taught her that. This keeps רבי אליעזר's opinion without insulting the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, say', which introduces a corrected reading
As if, it is considered as though

phrases.english: Rather, say:
it is as if he taught her promiscuity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: כְּאִילּוּ לִמְּדָהּ תִּיפְלוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wording seemed to call Torah itself תיפלות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Teaching her is only compared to teaching תיפלות. Torah itself is not תיפלות.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's source: wisdom brings cunning
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains רבי אליעזר's reason from the פסוק 'אני חכמה שכנתי ערמה': when wisdom enters a person, cunning enters with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: What is רבי אליעזר's reason? It is written, 'I, wisdom, dwell with cunning.' Once wisdom enters a person, cunning enters with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives the source and logic behind רבי אליעזר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says wisdom and ערמה, cunning, live together. So Torah learning brings sharpness, and רבי אליעזר worries she could use that sharpness to hide improper behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Cunning or shrewdness (it can also mean nakedness, as Step 6 shows)
Cunning, slyness

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?
As it is written: "I, wisdom, dwell with cunning,"
once wisdom enters a person,
cunning enters with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wording of רבי אליעזר's statement to its reason.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's view that teaching a daughter Torah is like teaching her תיפלות

steps.title: How do the רבנן read this פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן, who disagree with רבי אליעזר, learn from 'אני חכמה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this 'I, wisdom'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the other side explains the same פסוק, and sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק really means wisdom brings cunning, it seems to support רבי אליעזר. So the רבנן must read it differently, and the גמרא wants to know how.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who disagree with רבי אליעזר
What do they do with it? How do they use this source?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis,
this "I, wisdom," what do they do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי ״אֲנִי חׇכְמָה״ מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opposing view handles the פסוק brought in Step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן explain 'אני חכמה שכנתי ערמה' without agreeing with רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: Torah lasts in one who is 'bare' for it
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use the פסוק for רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's teaching. They read ערמה as nakedness: Torah lasts only in someone who makes himself bare for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for the teaching of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who said: Torah lasts only in a person who makes himself bare for it, as it says 'I, wisdom, dwell with ערמה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן read ערמה as 'nakedness' rather than 'cunning', so the פסוק teaches something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word ערמה can mean cunning or nakedness. For the רבנן, the פסוק teaches that Torah stays with someone ready to give up everything for it. So it says nothing against teaching women.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for (a different teaching)
Last, endure, stay with a person
Naked, bare

phrases.aramaic: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: He needs it for that of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina.
For Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
Words of Torah do not endure

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּמִי שֶׁמַּעֲמִיד עַצְמוֹ עָרוֹם עֲלֵיהֶן,
phrases.english: except in one who makes himself naked for them,
phrases.notes: Being 'naked' for Torah means being willing to give up all he owns for it.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "I, wisdom, dwell with nakedness."
phrases.notes: Same פסוק as before, משלי 8:12, but now ערמה is read as 'nakedness'.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן read ערמה as nakedness. The פסוק teaches that Torah lasts only in one who is ready to give up everything for it.
steps.confusionAlert: It is the same Hebrew word ערמה in both readings. רבי אליעזר reads it as 'cunning' and the רבנן read it as 'nakedness'. The disagreement depends on that one word.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Torah lasts in one who sees himself as nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds a similar teaching: Torah lasts only in someone who treats himself as if he does not exist. His source is 'והחכמה מאין תמצא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Torah lasts only in someone who makes himself like one who is not, as it says 'And wisdom, from nothingness it will be found.'
steps.whatsHappening: Once רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's teaching has come up, the גמרא brings a related teaching from רבי יוחנן about what it takes to hold on to Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads 'מאין', normally 'from where', as 'from nothingness'. Wisdom is found in a person who makes himself into nothing, meaning a truly humble person.

keyTerms.meaning: Like one who does not exist, as if he were nothing
Usually 'from where'; here read as 'from nothingness'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Words of Torah do not endure

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּמִי שֶׁמֵּשִׂים עַצְמוֹ כְּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ,
phrases.english: except in one who makes himself like one who is not,
as it is stated: "And wisdom, from nothingness it will be found."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִתְקַיְּימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related teaching that follows the pattern of Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah lasts only in someone with full humility, who treats himself as nothing.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to read 'אני חכמה שכנתי ערמה'. For רבי אליעזר, wisdom brings cunning. For the רבנן, Torah needs total self-giving. רבי יוחנן adds that Torah needs total humility.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's statement in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: רבי יהושע says, 'A woman prefers...'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: A woman prefers, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהושע's statement from the משנה so it can explain it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line in the משנה is short and unclear. Quoting it sets up the question that comes right after.

keyTerms.meaning: Wants, prefers

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
A woman prefers, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: רוֹצָה אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next statement in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע: a woman prefers a small amount with closeness over a large amount with separation (explained in Step 10).

steps.title: What does רבי יהושע mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהושע's short statement means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of רבי יהושע's words and sets up the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words of the משנה, 'a קב and תיפלות... nine קבין and פרישות', are unclear on their own. The גמרא wants them spelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? A request to explain unclear words

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the line quoted in Step 8 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of רבי יהושע's statement.

steps.title: One קב with closeness over nine קבין with separation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains: a woman prefers one קב of food together with her husband's closeness over nine קבין of food with separation.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is saying: A woman prefers one קב with physical closeness to nine קבין with separation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יהושע's words by filling in what the קב and the תיפלות refer to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קב is a measure of food, so this is about a small living compared to a rich one. רבי יהושע says a woman would choose less food if her husband is with her over much food with פרישות. This fits with the worry about teaching her Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is saying
A measure of volume, here of food
Separation, abstinence

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
A woman prefers a kav and intimacy with it,
phrases.notes: Here תיפלות means intimacy with her husband, not wrongdoing.

phrases.english: over nine kav and abstinence.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: רוֹצָה אִשָּׁה בְּקַב וְתִיפְלוּת עִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A woman would rather have one קב of food together with her husband's closeness than nine קבין of food with separation.
steps.confusionAlert: In Step 1, תיפלות meant promiscuity. Here it refers to closeness with her own husband.

steps.title: The next line of the משנה: the foolish pious man
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהושע's next teaching in the משנה, which opens with the חסיד שוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רבי יהושע) used to say: A foolish pious man, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה so it can explain it. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full line in the משנה lists several kinds of people who wear away the world. The גמרא quotes only the start and will now define the terms one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: A foolish pious man: someone whose 'piety' is so misguided that it causes harm
He used to say: introduces another teaching from the same תנא
Etc.: the rest of the quoted line is left out

phrases.english: He would say:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יהושע, from the line of the משנה quoted just before.

phrases.english: A foolish pious man, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יהושע's statement about a woman's preference to his next teaching in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Certain types of people, starting with the חסיד שוטה, wear away the world.

steps.title: What is a foolish pious man?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a concrete example of a חסיד שוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a foolish pious man like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of person the משנה means by a חסיד שוטה. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being pious sounds good, so it is unclear how a pious person could be harmful. The גמרא wants a real-life case that shows the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it like? A request for a concrete case

phrases.english: What is a foolish pious man like?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי חָסִיד שׁוֹטֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the first term in the quoted משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical example of a חסיד שוטה.

steps.title: The man who won't save a drowning woman
steps.stepSummary: A חסיד שוטה is someone who sees a woman drowning and refuses to save her, because he thinks it is improper to look at her.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, a woman is drowning in a river, and he says: It is not proper to look at her and save her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with an example: a man lets a woman drown because saving her would mean looking at her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His concern for modesty is real, but he applies it in the wrong place. Saving a life comes first, so his 'piety' leads to a death. That is what makes it foolish.

keyTerms.meaning: Is drowning
Proper conduct, the decent way to act
To look at

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a good value like modesty becomes harmful when it pushes aside saving a life.

phrases.english: For example, where a woman is drowning in a river,
and he says: It is not proper conduct
to look at her and save her.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן דְּקָא טָבְעָה אִיתְּתָא בְּנַהֲרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A man who lets a woman drown so that he won't have to look at her.

steps.title: What is a sly wicked person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for an example of the next type in the משנה, the רשע ערום.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a sly wicked person like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next term in the משנה and asks what a רשע ערום is. Several answers follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain wicked person is easy to spot. A sly one hides his wrongdoing, often behind actions that are legal, so the גמרא needs examples.

keyTerms.meaning: A sly or cunning wicked person who does wrong in a clever, hidden way

phrases.english: What is a sly wicked person like?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי רָשָׁע עָרוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first term in the משנה to the second.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical example of a רשע ערום.

steps.title: Speaking to the judge before the other side arrives
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן: a רשע ערום is someone who presents his side to the judge before the other party comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This is one who lays out his claims to the judge before the other party to the case arrives.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the first definition: a person who gets to the judge first and tells his story alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He has not lied or broken an obvious rule. But by speaking first, he shapes the judge's view before the other side can answer. The wrong is hidden, which is what makes him 'sly.'

keyTerms.meaning: Who lays out his claims, literally 'who gives a taste of his words'
Judge
The other party in the court case

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
This is one who lays out his claims to the judge
before the other party to the case comes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זֶה הַמַּטְעִים דְּבָרָיו לַדַּיָּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One who presents his case to the judge before the other side arrives.

steps.title: Giving a poor man one דינר to make him lose his gifts
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו: a רשע ערום gives a poor man one דינר to bring him up to 200 זוז, so that he can no longer take gifts for the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו says: This is one who gives a דינר to a poor man to complete two hundred זוז for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a second definition: someone who seems to do charity, but his one coin actually takes away the poor man's rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the outside it looks like kindness. In fact the gift pushes the poor man up to the cutoff, so he loses far more in gifts for the poor than the one דינר he received. The next step proves that this cutoff really exists.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin; the same value as a זוּז
To complete, to bring up to a full amount
Two hundred zuz, the cutoff for being counted as poor

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu says:
This is one who gives a dinar to a poor man
to complete two hundred zuz for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אוֹמֵר: זֶה הַנּוֹתֵן דִּינָר לְעָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One who gives a poor man a dinar to bring him up to 200 zuz.

steps.title: The משנה about the 200 זוז cutoff
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that someone with 200 זוז cannot take gifts for the poor, but someone with even one דינר less can take any amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: One who has two hundred זוז may not take לקט, שכחה, פאה, or מעשר עני. If he had two hundred less one דינר, even if they give him a thousand at once, he may take.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to show why רבי אבהו's case is so harmful. It proves the 200 זוז cutoff is real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At 199 זוז the poor man could collect a thousand at once. One extra דינר from the רשע ערום takes all of that away. So a tiny 'gift' causes a huge loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Gifts for the poor from the field: fallen stalks, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field
The tithe given to the poor
At once, all together

phrases.english: As we learned:
One who has two hundred zuz

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִטּוֹל לֶקֶט שִׁכְחָה וּפֵאָה וּמַעְשַׂר עָנִי.
phrases.english: may not take gleanings, forgotten sheaves, the corner of the field, or the poor man's tithe.
If he had two hundred less one dinar,
even if they give him a thousand at once,
he may take.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מָאתַיִם זוּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אבהו's definition by showing the law that makes his trick work.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבהו's claim that one dinar can make a poor man lose his gifts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה: someone with 200 zuz may not take gifts for the poor; someone with 199 may take even 1000 at once.

steps.title: Advising orphans to sell a small estate
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי in the name of רבי יוחנן: a רשע ערום advises orphans to sell from a small estate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is one who gives advice to sell from a small estate.
steps.whatsHappening: A third definition: someone who advises the orphan sons to sell from a small estate quickly. The next step shows why this works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a father leaves only a small estate, the daughters' support has a claim on it. By selling first, the sons keep the money and the daughters lose out. The advice is clever and legal, but it hurts the weaker side.

keyTerms.meaning: Who gives advice
A small estate, too small to support both sons and daughters

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
This is one who gives advice
to sell from a small estate.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זֶה הַמַּשִּׂיא עֵצָה לִמְכּוֹר בִּנְכָסִים מוּעָטִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One who advises orphans to sell from a small estate.

steps.title: Proof that the orphans' sale is valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's own ruling: if orphans went ahead and sold from a small estate, the sale stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Orphans who went ahead and sold from a small estate, what they sold, they sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling to show that the trick in the last step really works in law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sale were cancelled, the advice would do no harm. Because the sale stands, the daughters really lose their support. That is why the advisor counts as a רשע ערום.

keyTerms.meaning: Who went ahead, acted first
What they sold, they sold: the sale is valid

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Orphans who went ahead and sold from a small estate,
what they sold, they sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: יְתוֹמִים שֶׁקָּדְמוּ וּמָכְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the definition in step 18 by showing that such a sale is valid.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that advising orphans to sell early really harms the daughters.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a sale made early from a small estate stands.

steps.title: Advising a sale following רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: אביי: a רשע ערום advises someone to sell property in a way that only works according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is one who gives advice to sell property according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a fourth definition. The next step brings the ברייתא that explains which kind of sale he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case involves property given to one person and then, after him, to a second person. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that if the first one sells it, the sale stands, so advising him to sell cuts the second person out.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
This is one who gives advice to sell property
according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: זֶה הַמַּשִּׂיא עֵצָה לִמְכּוֹר בִּנְכָסִים כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth answer to the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One who advises a sale that works only according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: The ברייתא about 'my property to you, and after you to someone else'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: if the first heir sold the property, רבי says the second heir takes it back from the buyers, but רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the second gets only what the first left over.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'My property is to you, and after you to so-and-so.' If the first went ahead, sold it, and used up the money, the second takes it back from the buyers. These are the words of רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: The second gets only what the first left over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא behind אביי's definition. It shows that according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the first person's sale stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, the advice would not work, because the second person could take the property back. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל the sale holds, so whoever advises the first person to sell takes away what the giver meant for the second person. That legal-but-unfair move is what makes him a רשע ערום.

keyTerms.meaning: And after you, to so-and-so: the property passes to a second person
Buyers
What he left over

steps.whatToRemember: The first four definitions of a רשע ערום share one idea: he does something that looks proper, or is even legally valid, but uses it to hurt someone else.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not say רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows selling in the first place. The sale only stands after the fact, and advising someone to do it is the wicked part.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
"My property is to you, and after you to so-and-so,"
and the first went ahead and sold and used up the money,
the second takes it back from the buyers;
these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לַשֵּׁנִי אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁשִּׁיֵּיר רִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.english: The second has only what the first left over.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: נְכָסַי לְךָ, וְאַחֲרֶיךָ לִפְלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's definition by showing the ruling of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that advising such a sale causes real harm.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that the second person gets only what the first left over.

steps.title: Someone who pulls others into his ways
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר חמא, quoting רב ששת, defines a רשע ערום as someone who persuades others to follow his ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר חמא said in the name of רב ששת: A sly wicked person is someone who sways other people to act the way he acts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer to the question 'Who is a רשע ערום?' This time the answer is about a person's behavior, not a sly legal trick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers (steps 15-21) described clever moves, mostly legal ones, that hurt people. רב ששת's answer moves to a different kind of slyness: a person who looks good on the outside and gets others to copy him. That way his own faults stay hidden among everyone else, so they are hard to catch.

keyTerms.meaning: A sly, wicked person who hides his wickedness behind clever or proper-looking behavior
Tips the balance, sways or persuades
His ways, his manner of behaving

steps.confusionAlert: This answer is not about selling property anymore. The גמרא has moved from legal tricks to personal behavior.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Chama said in the name of Rav Sheshet:
This is one who sways others into his ways.
phrases.notes: 'This' is the רשע ערום the גמרא is trying to define.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: זֶה הַמַּכְרִיעַ אֲחֵרִים בְּאוֹרְחוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another parallel answer to the question of step 14, this time based on behavior rather than a legal trick.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who counts as a רשע ערום?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Someone who persuades others to follow his ways.

steps.title: Easy on himself, strict on others
steps.stepSummary: רבי זריקא, quoting רב הונא, defines a רשע ערום as someone who is lenient for himself and strict for others.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זריקא said in the name of רב הונא: A sly wicked person is someone who is easy on himself in הלכה but strict with other people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more answer to the same question: who is a רשע ערום?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person looks very frum because he makes others keep strict rules. In private he lets himself off easy. That gap between how he appears and how he really acts is exactly what makes him 'sly'.

keyTerms.meaning: Is lenient, takes the easy view
Is strict, takes the harder view
For himself

phrases.english: Rabbi Zerika said in the name of Rav Huna:
This is one who is lenient for himself
and strict for others.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: זֶה הַמֵּיקֵל לְעַצְמוֹ וּמַחְמִיר לַאֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further, separate definition of the same term, again about behavior.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who counts as a רשע ערום?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Someone who is lenient for himself and strict for others.

steps.title: עולא begins his definition
steps.stepSummary: עולא starts to give his own definition of a רשע ערום. His words continue past this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: This is... (his answer continues in the next part of the text).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up one more answer, from עולא. Only his opening words appear here; the rest of his definition comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the two answers before it, עולא's answer opens with 'זה', 'this is', pointing back to the רשע ערום. The content of his definition is not given yet, so we wait for the continuation.

phrases.english: Ulla said: This is

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא אָמַר: זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens yet another definition of רשע ערום, continuing the list of answers to step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who counts as a רשע ערום?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not yet stated; עולא's answer continues in the next section.
